en.name: John XIX
en.summary: A Tusculani pope, elevated directly from layman to pope in a single day, who crowned Conrad II emperor and briefly entertained a Byzantine primacy proposal.
en.body: John XIX, brother of his predecessor Benedict VIII and, like him, a layman before his election, was reportedly consecrated through the full clerical grades and installed as pope within a single day, reflecting the Tusculani family's direct control of the office. He crowned Conrad II emperor in 1027, and was said to have briefly considered a Byzantine proposal to recognize Constantinople's ecumenical primacy in the East before reversing course under Western clerical pressure.
